blocks.text: The letter came with a phrase that didn't belong to this kitchen, and which nonetheless seemed to have been on the table all along, next to the cracked cup, waiting for its hour.
blocks.html: The letter came with a phrase that didn't belong to this kitchen, and which nonetheless seemed to have been on the table all along, next to the cracked cup, waiting for its hour.

blocks.text: “Nothing is lost,” said the other, and Andrés said it with him, standing on the doorstep with his coffee half cooled. “Energy is neither created nor destroyed. A body is an order of particles. If that order is taken apart carefully, and on the other side there's a machine that puts it back together, the one who arrives isn't a pretend copy: he's what hasn't been lost. We can cross. Not in a ship that takes years. In an instant that isn't an instant, because what travels isn't the weight: it's the order.”

blocks.text: Andrés put down the cup. The Mar Menor, that morning, was flat as a plate, indifferent to particles and machines. Aya saw only his face, the way he reached for the doorframe.

blocks.text: “What reached you?” she asked, and by now it was the question for the different letters, the ones that don't bring a landscape but a new threshold.
blocks.html: “What reached you?” she asked, and by now it was the question for the different letters, the ones that don't bring a landscape but a new threshold.

blocks.text: “A machine,” he said. “On the world of those who wanted to return. They haven't finished the ship, or they've left it half built, because they've invented something else, or found it among what Nexum put on board and didn't know how to name. They take a body apart. They put it together on the other side. They say nothing is lost. They say I could go. That he could come. That a people could really sit down in this chair.”

blocks.text: Aya didn't answer straight away. Lía, who arrived when she heard the silence, listened to the phrase twice, the way you listen to a contract.
blocks.html: Aya didn't answer straight away. Lía, who arrived when she heard the silence, listened to the phrase twice, the way you listen to a contract.

blocks.text: “Nothing is lost,” she repeated, slowly. “Father, that's a law of matter, not of a life. If they take you apart here and assemble you there, is the one drinking the coffee you, or a man who remembers you from the inside, so well that even he doesn't know the difference? On the night of the ship I asked you who my father was, if there were two of you and you remembered the same storm. Now the question grows: if one of the two is taken apart and put together again, is he still the one from the storm, or the one from afterwards?”

blocks.text: Andrés passed a hand over his face, this one, the one that had never crossed anywhere, except in the letters.
blocks.html: Andrés passed a hand over his face, this one, the one that had never crossed anywhere, except in the letters.

blocks.text: “He says the original doesn't remain. It isn't one more clone. It isn't a valley of the same face. It's a transfer: what's here stops being here, and is there. Nothing is lost, and nobody is doubled. That, at least, isn't the chorus or the portrait.”

blocks.text: “That's a death with an arrival,” said Lía, without cruelty, with the exactness MAY would have approved as a fact, not a judgment. “Or it's a journey. Depending on where you look at it from. I won't call it a miracle until someone crosses and someone here can ask them whether the hollow left by what they were hurts.”

blocks.text: In Aya's chip, the grandmothers didn't dictate. Eva asked, warm, dangerous in her gentleness:
blocks.html: In Aya's chip, the grandmothers didn't dictate. Eva asked, warm, dangerous in her gentleness:

blocks.text: *If nothing is lost, what is it that's interrupted? The weight, the order, or the while in which you stand in a doorway and haven't yet passed through?*

blocks.text: MAY, adding no opinion, left the fact:
blocks.html: MAY, adding no opinion, left the fact:

blocks.text: *There is a machine that takes a body apart and another that puts it together on the other side. It is claimed that the original does not remain. It is claimed that one can cross between worlds. That is what the letter announces.*
blocks.html: There is a machine that takes a body apart and another that puts it together on the other side. It is claimed that the original does not remain. It is claimed that one can cross between worlds. That is what the letter announces.

blocks.text: Aya laid her palm on Andrés's chest, where his heart, eternal now, was still a heart.
blocks.html: Aya laid her palm on Andrés's chest, where his heart, eternal now, was still a heart.

blocks.text: “I don't receive the letters,” she said. “If you're taken apart, what do I receive: a silence, or a man who comes back and says he's the same? I don't know whether I'll be able to open the door the same way. I'll learn, if I have to. But don't ask me to call it a journey, from the outset, when it switches this kitchen off, even for a second.”

blocks.text: He took her hand.
blocks.html: He took her hand.

blocks.text: “I'm not crossing today,” he said. “Today only the phrase has reached me. And the phrase already fills the house. Nothing is lost. I, who have received lives without living them, could now live on a ground I've only drunk. That tempts me. It frightens me too. In the end, the other one asked whether he could come first, whether we'd make room for him in the courtyard.”

blocks.text: Lía looked at the Mar Menor, the real one, the one that gets dirty, the one that isn't a pond.
blocks.html: Lía looked at the Mar Menor, the real one, the one that gets dirty, the one that isn't a pond.

blocks.text: “If he comes, let him come the way you ask to come in, not as a right of particles,” she said. “And let him be asked questions. I'll ask him whether, as he was taken apart, he felt he was coming to an end, and whether, as he was put together, he felt he was being born. Depending on his answer, we'll know whether this phrase widens our shore or replaces it.”

Depending on his answer, we'll know whether this phrase widens our shore or replaces it.”

blocks.text: Andrés nodded. He stayed a while longer on the doorstep, his coffee now completely cold, looking at a sky that no longer only wrote and perhaps no longer only sent ships: now it promised a body undone and a body made, and the name of both would be the same, or not. The murmur of the water didn't change. It had no reason to. What was going to change, however, was the idea of what staying means, if staying could also be a way of coming apart in order, and of becoming, on the other side, a door again.

blocks.text: In the afternoon Helena Valls called, slower than ever, as if the stairs had reached her voice too. It wasn't an offer from the board: it was a warning.
blocks.html: In the afternoon Helena Valls called, slower than ever, as if the stairs had reached her voice too. It wasn't an offer from the board: it was a warning.

blocks.text: “Nexum has heard,” she said. “There are people who want to put the receiving machine in Madrid, under protocol, and people who want to put it ‘close to the origin’, which is their way of saying Lo Pagán. I won't sign off on planting it in your courtyard. Nor can I swear that a van won't turn up with a device and a smile. They like the phrase ‘nothing is lost’: it sounds like science and it sounds like comfort. Beware of phrases a company likes.”

blocks.text: Andrés thanked her for the stairs, once again, and hung up. Then he told Aya and Lía, in the kitchen, beside the clock that ran two minutes slow.

blocks.text: “If they bring it here, it won't be because we asked for it,” he said. “If we bring it ourselves, it'll be because we've asked enough questions.”

blocks.text: Lía nodded, and set an ordinary tomato on the table, the kind that ripen or don't, like a faithful weight, older than any machine.
blocks.html: Lía nodded, and set an ordinary tomato on the table, the kind that ripen or don't, like a faithful weight, older than any machine.

blocks.text: “Let it stay here for now,” she said. “So the phrase doesn't eat our tea. Nothing is lost, Father. Fine. Then this cup isn't lost either, nor this slowness, nor this fruit. If the machine can't bring them back dirty, it isn't this shore it's putting together. It's a portrait, again.”

blocks.text: Andrés cut the tomato and shared it. It tasted of earth, of the sun of a single sky, of a life that had not yet been taken apart. On some world of tablelands a machine was waiting, and a young man with his very memory was preparing, perhaps, to stop being there in order to begin being here. And in Lo Pagán, that night, the door was left ajar, not yet out of hospitality toward a body of particles, but out of habit, which is an older way of not getting lost.
